title: Manage Nucleus agent jobs and service
summary: Check readiness and account access, submit or inspect agent jobs, read their output, cancel work, or operate the per-user Nucleus service.
use_when: Nucleus readiness, authentication, job state, exact harness output, cancellation, or service state must be inspected or changed.
An exact version-one invocation must be submitted directly for technical diagnosis or a deliberate runtime task.
do_not_use_when: The request is ordinary immediate work that the current interactive agent can perform directly.
A requester-owned domain result or retry decision is the actual authority being sought.
The goal is to create a project registry or workflow graph.
outcome: A clearly observed or deliberately changed Nucleus runtime condition, identified through Nucleus job, account, service, or health state rather than requester domain inference.
effects: Read commands expose daemon, account, job, request, and exact harness-output state.
Job submission creates one durable Nucleus job and may invoke Codex and consume account allowance.
Cancellation records intent for one exact job attempt; authentication login changes the Nucleus-owned credential.
Service restart makes every unfinished attempt lost, while uninstall removes installed programs but retains state and logs.
authority: Nucleus owns admission, one harness attempt per job, job lifecycle, cancellation, the credential lease, exact harness stdout, and the durable requester-tool mailbox.
The requester remains authoritative for the domain result, idempotency, and whether a new attempt is safe.
success: The requested Nucleus state is confirmed through the corresponding supported CLI response.
For direct submission, the exact request is admitted under its job ID and the required runtime observation is obtained.
Requester domain success is verified separately whenever the job belongs to an application.
failure_and_recovery: If health cannot connect, inspect `nucleus service status` and the user-service logs; do not create a hidden direct-Codex fallback.
If authentication is unavailable, quiesce requesters before attended device login and run a deliberate requester canary afterward.
If an attempt is lost or fails after a domain commit, inspect requester state before considering any new job.
privacy: Nucleus state may contain complete prompts, tool arguments and results, source content, exact app-server stdout, and authentication material.
The per-user socket relies on local filesystem ownership rather than application-level authentication.
does_not_authorize: A new requester attempt after failure or loss.
Acceptance of any Todo, Annals, Weaver, or other requester-owned domain result.
Restarting or uninstalling the service while active attempts matter.
